title: How a cell makes and secretes a protein
caption: A secreted protein such as insulin follows one route through the endomembrane system: made on ribosomes of the rough ER, folded inside it, modified in the Golgi and released by exocytosis. Mitochondria supply the ATP but are not part of the route.
alt: Seven boxes in order: nucleus, ribosome on the rough endoplasmic reticulum, rough ER, transport vesicle, Golgi apparatus, secretory vesicle and plasma membrane.
description: Nucleus: the gene is copied into mRNA.
Ribosome on the rough ER: translates the mRNA into a polypeptide.
Rough ER: the chain is threaded in, folded and given sugars.
Transport vesicle: buds off and carries it to the Golgi.
Golgi apparatus: modifies it from the cis face to the trans face.
Secretory vesicle: carries it to the cell surface.
Plasma membrane: the vesicle fuses: exocytosis releases it.
Lysosomal enzymes leave the same route at the Golgi, tagged with mannose-6-phosphate.
